- Overestimate prices in the short term after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative; model often fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < 0.3), model forecasts should be reduced by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.
- If recent price history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops), model should not assume continuation; apply mean reversion bias.
- Overshoots after spikes are common in the 10–15 day window; apply a 2–3 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is high but price action is volatile — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% if sentiment > 0.7 and volatility > 0.15.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly trending — if sentiment is flat or mixed, assume 1–2% mean reversion per day.
